receivedItems.description: Jon Rahm said Tuesday that if offered the same deal Brooks Koepka got to return to the PGA Tour, he'd be willing to accept the penalties.

images.name: PGA Tour CEO: LIV golfers would have to earn their way in, just like any other player
images.caption: PGA Tour CEO: LIV golfers would have to earn their way in, just like any other player

receivedItems.headline: Fifa Laopakdee wins Asia-Pacific Amateur, earns Masters, Open Championship bids
receivedItems.description: Three shots behind with 10 holes to play, Fifa Laopakdee rallied to become the second player to win back-to-back Asia-Pacific Amateur titles.

images.name: Golfball 140910 [600x400]
images.alt: Golfball

receivedItems.headline: Swanwick surges to Asia-Pacific lead after defending champ Laopakdee fades
receivedItems.description: Zack Swanwick shot a 4-under 67 to take a two-shot lead in the Asia-Pacific Amateur after Fifa Laopakdee struggled on the back nine and settled for a 73.

images.name: Golfball 140910 [600x400]
images.alt: Golfball

receivedItems.headline: BYU sophomore Akina, 20, fires 64 to grab share of Mexico Open lead
receivedItems.description: Kihei Akina, a 20-year-old sophomore at BYU, was part of a three-way tie atop the leaderboard in the Mexico Open after shooting a 7-under 64 on Friday.

receivedItems.headline: Fifa Laopakdee salvages 71 for 2-shot lead in windy Asia-Pacific Amateur
receivedItems.description: Fifa Laopakdee followed his opening-round 63 with a 71 on Friday to take a two-stroke lead in the Asia-Pacific Amateur Championship in New Zealand.

images.name: Golfball 140910 [600x400]
images.alt: Golfball

receivedItems.headline: Karl Vilips shoots 62, takes first-round Mexico Open lead
receivedItems.description: Karl Vilips used two long bridie streaks to take the first-round lead Thursday in the Mexico Open, the first of two straight PGA Tour events in the country.

images.name: Karl Vilips [600x400]
images.caption: Karl Vilips shot a 9-under 62 in the first round of the Mexico Open on Thursday, making five straight birdies on Nos. 11-15 on his opening nine and finishing with four in a row.

receivedItems.headline: Sergio Garcia leaving LIV Golf, returning to DP World Tour
receivedItems.description: Sergio Garcia, the 2017 Masters champion, is leaving the LIV Golf League and returning to the DP World Tour, he announced on social media Thursday.

images.name: Sergio García takes frustration out on driver after poor tee shot
images.caption: Sergio Garcia snaps the head of his driver in frustration after his tee shot on Hole 2 of the Masters.

receivedItems.headline: Sources: Tiger Woods expected to play in TGL opener Dec. 27
receivedItems.description: Tiger Woods, barring another physical setback, is expected to compete in Jupiter Links GC's season-opening match when TGL kicks off Dec. 27, sources told ESPN.

images.name: Tiger Woods [1296x729]
images.caption: Jupiter Links Golf Club lost to New York Golf Club, 10-3 on Tuesday night.
images.credit: Photo by Megan Briggs/TGL/TGL via Getty Images

images.name: Tom Kim celebrates with Tiger Woods after hole-in-one at TGL
images.caption: Tom Kim sinks a hole-in-one to give Jupiter Links a 7-6 lead heading into the final hole.

receivedItems.headline: Smotherman wins Bermuda Championship, earns U.S. Open berth
receivedItems.description: Austin Smotherman captured his second straight FedEx Cup Fall event Monday morning when he outlasted Seamus Power of Ireland with a par on the third playoff hole to win the rain-shortened Butterfield Bermuda Championship.

receivedItems.headline: Yuto Katsuragawa wins Genesis Championship for second DP World Tour title
receivedItems.description: Yuto Katsuragawa secured his second DP World Tour title with a two-shot victory at the Genesis Championship in South Korea.

receivedItems.headline: LIV Golf's Scott O'Neil given $6.3M before bankruptcy protection filing
receivedItems.description: LIV Golf CEO Scott O'Neil was given a retention payment of $6.375 million less than three months before the tour filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection.

images.name: 260819 ONeil [1296x729]
images.caption: LIV CEO Scott O'Neil remained bullish about plans for 2027 and beyond, saying players would be equity owners and have their commercial rights restored. "We have work to do," he said, "... but man, I wouldn't bet against us."

images.name: PGA Tour CEO: LIV golfers would have to earn their way in, just like any other player
images.caption: PGA Tour CEO: LIV golfers would have to earn their way in, just like any other player

receivedItems.headline: Chandler Blanchet and Kensei Hirata share the lead in Bermuda
receivedItems.description: Chandler Blanchet and Kensei Hirata of Japan share the lead going into the weekend at the Butterfield Bermuda Championship.

receivedItems.headline: Ian Poulter, Tyrrell Hatton won't be part of LIV Golf 2.0
receivedItems.description: Ian Poulter and Tyrrell Hatton are among a group of golfers who announced Friday that they won't be a part of LIV Golf 2.0.

images.name: Ian Poulter [1296x729]
images.alt: Ian Poulter

receivedItems.headline: Jarvis shares halfway lead with Rozner at Genesis Championship
receivedItems.description: With his sights on the season-long Race to Dubai title, South African golfer Casey Jarvis shot 4-under 67 in the second round of the Genesis Championship to share the lead with Antoine Rozner in the European tour event on Friday.

receivedItems.headline: Chandler Blanchet rides pair of eagles to lead in Bermuda
receivedItems.description: Chandler Blanchet made a pair of eagles to post his best score of the year -- a 9-under 62 -- on Thursday.

receivedItems.headline: Blades Brown, Ben James join Jackson Koivun as new TGL golfers for 2027 season
receivedItems.description: Blades Brown and Ben James are joining PGA Tour rookie Jackson Koivun as new competitors in the third TGL season.

receivedItems.headline: Eugenio Chacarra wins DP World India Championship, now No. 1 in Race to Dubai
receivedItems.description: Eugenio Chacarra won the DP World India Championship to maintain a late-season surge that has lifted the Spanish golfer atop the Race to Dubai standings.

receivedItems.headline: Patrick Reed on India cut line; McIlroy, Chacarra rounds halted by darkness
receivedItems.description: Patrick Reed is sitting on the projected cut line at DP World India Championship after play was suspended due to darkness with half the field still to finish the second round.

receivedItems.headline: Jon Rahm reaches separation deal with LIV, gives up rest of nine-figure contract
receivedItems.description: Jon Rahm and LIV Golf have reached a separation agreement in which Rahm agreed to release all of his monetary and economic claims in exchange for the return of his exclusive name, image and likeness rights and other related marks.

images.name: Jon Rahm [600x400]
images.caption: Jon Rahm is looking for his third major title.

receivedItems.description: Will Zalatoris told reporters Wednesday that he will undergo spinal fusion surgery next month and will miss all of 2027.

images.name: Zalatoris reacts [600x600]
images.caption: Zalatoris finished in last place at the Hero World Challenge and missed cut at the Sony Open.
images.alt: Will Zalatoris of the United States reacts after making a birdie

receivedItems.headline: LIV Golf to know its future by end of month, attorney says
receivedItems.description: Robert Fitzgerald, an attorney representing LIV Golf in a bankruptcy hearing, said they'd know by Oct. 31 if they'd "wind down or whether 2.0 is going forward."

receivedItems.description: Jackson Koivun has been selected to take part in the Skins Game on Nov. 27, along with Brooks Koepka, Justin Thomas and U.S. Open champion Wyndham Clark.

images.name: Jackson Koivun [1296x729]
images.caption: Jackson Koivun is currently No. 70 in the FedEx Cup standings.

receivedItems.headline: Michael Brennan takes Baycurrent for 2nd PGA Tour win of season
receivedItems.description: Michael Brennan scored a one-shot win over Jacob Bridgeman and Keith Mitchell at the Baycurrent Classic for his second PGA Tour victory of the season.

receivedItems.headline: Scott, Thomas move into contention at PGA Tour's Baycurrent Classic
receivedItems.description: Adam Scott and Justin Thomas moved into contention at the PGA Tour's Baycurrent Classic, with both one stroke off the lead after three rounds at the Yokohama Country Club.

images.name: Adam Scott [600x400]
images.credit: Photo by Yu Chun Christopher Wong/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images

receivedItems.headline: Bridgeman (-8) holds one-shot lead at Baycurrent Classic in Japan
receivedItems.description: Jacob Bridgeman birdied four of his last five holes Thursday for an 8-under 63 to take a one-shot lead over Jordan Smith in the Baycurrent Classic in Yokohama, Japan.

images.name: Jacob Bridgeman [600x400]
images.credit: Yu Chun Christopher Wong/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images

receivedItems.description: Two-time major champion Jon Rahm is leaving the LIV Golf League and is working to finalize a separation agreement by Oct. 15, his attorney said.

receivedItems.headline: Lindy Duncan's long-awaited first LPGA Tour win comes at The Annika
receivedItems.description: Lindy Duncan, 35, became the oldest first-time winner on the LPGA Tour since Leta Lindley was 36 when she won the Corning Classic in 2008.

images.name: Lindy Duncan  [600x600]
images.caption: Lindy Duncan, 35, became the oldest first-time winner on the LPGA Tour since 2008.

receivedItems.headline: Lindy Duncan plays it safe in bogey-free, 17-par round, up 1 shot in The Annika
receivedItems.description: Lindy Duncan made 17 pars in a bogey-free round and finished with a 1-under 69 and a one-shot lead in The Annika.

receivedItems.headline: Hye-Jin Choi, Carlota Ciganda, Lindy Duncan share lead at The Annika
receivedItems.description: Hye-Jin Choi opened with two bogeys, made up ground with a 15-foot eagle putt late and finished with a 3-under 67 Friday that gave her a three-way share of the lead at The Annika and another chance to win for the first time in 127 tries on the LPGA Tour.

receivedItems.headline: Nelly Korda 2 shots back at LPGA Tour's The Annika
receivedItems.description: Nelly Korda played bogey-free Thursday at The Annika and opened with a 7-under 65 to trail Minami Katsu and Hye-Jin Choi by two shots.

receivedItems.headline: LPGA's Ryann O'Toole grabs $1 million bonus while awaiting birth of first child
receivedItems.description: Veteran LPGA golfer Ryann O'Toole will get a $1M for winning the Aon Risk Reward Challenge, a bonus program built around a player's average score on a designated hole.

images.name: Ryann O'Toole [1296x729] - Copy 20261109
images.caption: Ryann O'Toole of The U.S. won her first LPGA Tour event in 228 starts, the Women's Scottish Open at Dumbarnie Links, Scotland.

receivedItems.headline: Shuri Sakuma cruises to 4-shot Japan Classic victory for first LPGA Tour title
receivedItems.description: Shuri Sakuma scored a four-stroke victory in the Toto Japan Classic after firing a final-round 64 for her first LPGA Tour title.

receivedItems.headline: Aki Iwai shoots 66, takes 1-shot lead into final round of LPGA's Japan Classic
receivedItems.description: Aki Iwai shot a 6-under 66 and was one shot clear of Arpichaya Yubol heading into the final round of the LPGA's Toto Japan Classic.

receivedItems.headline: Defending champ Nasa Hataoka rides eagle on 17th to 1-shot lead at LPGA Japan
receivedItems.description: Nasa Hataoka fired an 8-under 64, highlighted by an eagle on the par-5 17th hole, to take a one-shot lead Friday at the Toto Japan Classic.

receivedItems.headline: Nelly Korda clinches LPGA player of the year, moves closer to Hall of Fame
receivedItems.description: Nelly Korda clinched the points-based LPGA player of the year on Tuesday, her second such award in three years and moving her one victory away from qualifying for the LPGA Hall of Fame.

images.name: Nelly Korda [600x400]
images.caption: Nelly Korda clinched LPGA player of the year when double major winner Haeran Ryu had to withdraw last week in Malaysia due to injury, and Miyu Yamashita and Jeeno Thitikul did not enter The Annika next week in Florida.

receivedItems.headline: Miyu Yamashita holds off Yan Liu to defend LPGA Maybank Championship title
receivedItems.description: Miyu Yamashita successfully defended her title at the LPGA Tour's Maybank Championship, beating China's Yan Liu by two strokes.

receivedItems.headline: Defending champion Yamashita maintains lead after 3 rounds at LPGA Malaysia
receivedItems.description: Defending champion Miyu Yamashita shot a 5-under 67 to take a two-stroke lead into Sunday's final round of the LPGA Tour's Maybank Championship.

receivedItems.headline: Defending champion Yamashita leads LPGA's Maybank Championship after 2 rounds
receivedItems.description: Defending champion and world No. 4-ranked Miyu Yamashita shot a 6-under 66 to take a two-stroke lead after two rounds of the LPGA Tour's Maybank Championship.

images.name: Miyu Yamashita [600x400]
images.credit: Photo by Yong Teck Lim/Getty Images

receivedItems.headline: Pauline Roussin-Bouchard birdies last three holes, leads Maybank Classic by 1
receivedItems.description: Pauline Roussin-Bouchard birdied her final three holes for an 8-under 64 and a one-stroke lead after the first round of the LPGA Tour's Maybank Classic.

receivedItems.headline: Haeran Ryu withdraws from LPGA Tour's Maybank Classic
receivedItems.description: Haeran Ryu withdrew from the LPGA Tour's Maybank Classic before her first round Thursday.

receivedItems.headline: Yuri Yoshida wins in South Korea for first LPGA Tour victory
receivedItems.description: Yuri Yoshida won the LPGA South Korea tournament after holding off Haeran Ryu and Hye-Jin Choi in a close finish at Pine Beach Golf Links.

receivedItems.headline: Hye-Jin Choi moves into second-place tie at LPGA South Korea
receivedItems.description: Hye-Jin Choi had an eagle and seven birdies in her first 11 holes on a rain-soaked Pine Beach Golf Links to shoot a 6-under 66 and move into tie for second place after three rounds of the LPGA South Korea tournament.

receivedItems.headline: Haeran Ryu takes 2-stroke, 2nd-round lead at LPGA's South Korea event
receivedItems.description: Haeran Ryu had two eagles and birdied her final two holes for an 8-under 64 Friday to take a two-stroke lead after 36 holes of the LPGA South Korea tournament.

receivedItems.headline: Davidson, Yoshida tied for 1st-round lead at LPGA South Korea tournament
receivedItems.description: Karis Davidson had six birdies in eight holes but bogeyed her ninth Thursday for a 6-under 66 and was tied for the first-round lead in South Korea.

receivedItems.headline: Ruoning Yin overtakes Hye-Jin Choi with late birdie for LPGA Shanghai win
receivedItems.description: Ruoning Yin made a four-foot birdie putt on the 16th hole to break out of a back-nine tie with third-round leader Hye-Jin Choi and win the LPGA Shanghai tournament by one stroke.

receivedItems.headline: Hye-Jin Choi retains lead after three rounds of LPGA Shanghai
receivedItems.description: Hye-Jin Choi extended her tournament-long lead by shooting a 3-under 69 to take a one-stroke advantage into the final round of the LPGA Shanghai event.

receivedItems.headline: Hye-Jin Choi maintains lead after two rounds of LPGA Shanghai
receivedItems.description: Hye-Jin Choi overcame difficult scoring conditions to shoot a 2-over 74 but still maintained a two-stroke lead after two rounds of the LPGA Shanghai tournament.

receivedItems.headline: Hye-Jin Choi takes 1st-round lead at Shanghai LPGA event
receivedItems.description: Hye-Jin Choi shot an 8-under 64 to take a three-stroke lead after the first round of the Shanghai event.

receivedItems.headline: LPGA's '27 schedule features higher purses, better travel efficiency
receivedItems.description: The LPGA Tour 2027 schedule will feature 33 tournaments, a record $147 million in prize money and a more efficient travel itinerary for its players.

receivedItems.headline: Jeeno Thitikul wins in Hawaii for her 4th LPGA Tour victory of the season
receivedItems.description: Jeeno Thitikul of Thailand quickly overcame a late double bogey to win the LOTTE Championship for her fourth LPGA Tour victory of the season.

receivedItems.headline: Jeeno Thitikul, Polly Mack birdie 18th for share of lead in Honolulu
receivedItems.description: Second-ranked Jeeno Thitikul of Thailand made a 12-foot birdie putt on the par-5 18th for a 7-under 65 a share of the second-round lead Friday in the LPGA Tour's LOTTE Championship.

receivedItems.headline: A Lim Kim fires 65 at rainy Hoakalei to take lead in LOTTE Championship
receivedItems.description: A Lim Kim shot a 7-under 65 on a rainy and breezy Thursday at Hoakalei to take the first-round lead in the LPGA Tour's LOTTE Championship.

receivedItems.headline: Butch Harmon, Dottie Pepper among Hall of Fame finalists
receivedItems.description: Butch Harmon and Dottie Pepper, who came close to induction two years ago, are among the 14 finalists for the 2027 World Golf Hall of Fame induction class.

images.name: Golf HOF 141216 [600x400]
images.alt: World Golf Hall of Fame

receivedItems.headline: Japan's Yuna Nishimura wins LPGA Tour's Walmart NW Arkansas
receivedItems.description: Yuna Nishimura played a flawless back nine after allowing the chasing pack to get close early and won the Walmart NW Arkansas Championship by five shots on Sunday for her first LPGA victory.

images.name: Yuna Nishimura [600x600]
images.caption: Yuna Nishimura celebrates after winning the Walmart NW Arkansas Championship on Sunday.

receivedItems.headline: Coughlin first in LPGA history to open round with 9 straight birdies
receivedItems.description: Lauren Coughlin made LPGA history when she birdied her first nine holes at the Walmart NW Arkansas Championship on Saturday.

images.name: Lauren Coughlin [600x400]
images.caption: Lauren Coughlin's nine straight birdies keyed a second-round 61 on Saturday, moving her up 106 spots on the leaderboard into a tie for 21st.

receivedItems.headline: Team Europe reclaims Solheim Cup with Sunday splash over U.S.
receivedItems.description: The Solheim Cup is back in the hands of the Europeans after Lottie Woad holed a putt from 2 feet on No. 17 to guarantee Team Europe would reach the 14½ points needed to beat the United States.

receivedItems.headline: Jennifer Kupcho sinks unlikely putts to even Solheim Cup
receivedItems.description: Jennifer Kupcho rolled in two late birdie putts -- one from 93 feet -- to earn the Americans an unlikely point and tie the Solheim Cup at 8-8 after four sessions.

images.name: 260912 jennifer kupcho photo [1296x729]
images.caption: Jennifer Kupcho celebrates after sinking a second straight long putt to win her match and even the Solheim Cup.

receivedItems.headline: Europe builds 7-5 lead at Solheim Cup after Korda, Corpuz falter
receivedItems.description: Team Europe finally took down the record-setting U.S. partnership of Nelly Korda and Allisen Corpuz at the Solheim Cup on the way to winning the morning foursomes and building a 7-5 lead after three sessions.

receivedItems.headline: Solheim Cup: Europe, U.S. tied 4-4 after Ciganda's late heroics
receivedItems.description: Europe's Carlota Ciganda pulled off an unlikely par after Americans Nelly Korda and Lauren Coughlin left birdie putts short to gain a half-point with rookie Julia Lopez Ramirez and leave the teams tied at 4-4 after Day 1 at the Solheim Cup.

receivedItems.headline: Europe, U.S. tied at 2-2 after opening session of Solheim Cup
receivedItems.description: Nelly Korda played like the world No. 1 in a record-setting partnership with Allisen Corpuz, helping the Americans split the opening foursomes 2-2 with Team Europe in a loud and wet start to the Solheim Cup.

receivedItems.headline: Solheim Cup to begin with Nelly Korda-Charley Hull matchup
receivedItems.description: Europe's top two players, Charley Hull and Lottie Woad, will open the Solheim Cup against a U.S. pairing containing top-ranked Nelly Korda.

images.name: Nelly Korda [600x400]
images.caption: Nelly Korda hits her drive on the first hole of the final round of the U.S. Women's Open.
images.alt: Nelly Korda

receivedItems.headline: Ruoning Yin birdies 18 to take the 1-shot lead at TPC Boston
receivedItems.description: Ruoning Yin chipped in for birdie from just off the 18th green to take the third-round lead Saturday at TPC Boston in the FM Championship.

receivedItems.headline: Miyu Yamashita keeps rolling, shares 2nd-round lead at FM Championship
receivedItems.description: Miyu Yamashita was back on top of an LPGA Tour leaderboard days after tying the tour's 72-hole scoring record in a nine-stroke victory in Canada.

images.name: 260820 Yamashita [600x400]
images.caption: Miyu Yamashita ended her Thursday morning round at Royal Mayfair atop the leaderboard -- despite the abundance of mosquitoes on the course.

receivedItems.headline: Sei Young Kim shoots 64 for 1st-round lead in FM Championship
receivedItems.description: Sei Young Kim capped a second-nine spree with a chip-in eagle and shot an 8-under 64 on Thursday at the TPC Boston to take the first-round lead in the FM Championship.

receivedItems.headline: LPGA Tour announces plans for Hong Kong event next year
receivedItems.description: The LPGA Tour and presenting sponsor Moomoo announced plans Wednesday for an event in Hong Kong beginning next year.

receivedItems.headline: 3-time major champ, Solheim captain Anna Nordqvist retiring
receivedItems.description: Three-time major champion Anna Nordqvist will retire as a player after this weekend's FM Championship in Boston, saying she will pivot to focus on her health and family.

receivedItems.headline: Miyu Yamashita matches LPGA Tour 72-hole scoring record in CPKC win
receivedItems.description: Japanese star Miyu Yamashita matched the LPGA Tour's 72-hole scoring record Sunday in a wire-to-wire, nine-stroke victory in the CPKC Women's Open at Royal Mayfair.

receivedItems.headline: Yamashita's CPKC Women's Open lead up to 6 shots after 65
receivedItems.description: Miyu Yamashita will bid for a wire-to-wire victory after stretching her lead in the CPKC Women's Open to six shots following a 5-under 65 on Saturday.

receivedItems.headline: Yamashita widens CPKC Women's Open lead to 5 shots after 64
receivedItems.description: After an opening-round 62, Miyu Yamashita shot 64 on Friday afternoon to open a five-shot lead in the CPKC Women's Open.

images.name: Miyu Yamashita [600x400]
images.credit: Darryl Dyck/The Canadian Press via AP

receivedItems.headline: Miyu Yamashita opens with 62 to lead CPKC Women's Open
receivedItems.description: Miyu Yamashita shot an 8-under 62 on Thursday for a one-stroke lead over fellow Japanese player Nasa Hataoka in the CPKC Women's Open, with two Canadian teenagers on the leaderboard in the national championship.

images.name: 260820 Yamashita [600x400]
images.caption: Miyu Yamashita ended her Thursday morning round at Royal Mayfair atop the leaderboard -- despite the abundance of mosquitoes on the course.

receivedItems.headline: Jeeno Thitikul rallies with final-round 64 to win in Portland
receivedItems.description: Jeeno Thitikul ran off five straight birdies early and closed with an 8-under 64 for a one-shot victory Sunday in The Standard Portland Classic, her third LPGA Tour title of the season.

images.name: Jeeno Thitikul LPGA Portland_260816 [1296x729]
images.caption: Jeeno Thitikul won the The Standard Portland Classic on Sunday for her third LPGA Tour victory of the season.
images.alt: Jeeno Thitikul won the The Standard Portland Classic on Sunday for her third LPGA Tour victory of the season.

receivedItems.headline: Sophia Schubert, Arpichaya Yubol share 2-shot lead in Portland
receivedItems.description: Sophia Schubert birdied two of the final three holes for a 5-under 67 and a share of the lead with Arpichaya Yubol on Saturday in The Standard Portland Classic.

receivedItems.headline: Arpichaya Yubol takes LPGA Tour lead into weekend in Portland
receivedItems.description: Arpichaya Yubol shot her second straight 6-under 66 to take the second-round lead in The Standard Portland Classic.

receivedItems.headline: Mariel Galdiano leads Portland Classic by 1 shot
receivedItems.description: Mariel Galdiano posted a 7-under 65 in one of the first groups Thursday in The Standard Portland Classic, and watched it hold up for a one-stroke lead.

receivedItems.headline: Inkster Award-winner Megha Ganne to make LPGA debut in Portland
receivedItems.description: Megha Ganne makes her LPGA debut as a pro this week at The Standard Portland Classic with an exemption from winning the Inkster Award.

images.name: 260811 Ganne [1296x729]
images.caption: Megha Ganne, a four-time All-America at Stanford who won the U.S. Women's Amateur, will make her LPGA debut at The Standard Portland Classic this week.

receivedItems.headline: Asterisk Talley wins U.S. Women's Amateur for 2nd USGA title
receivedItems.description: Asterisk Talley picked up her biggest win yet Sunday when she surged past Anna Iwanaga of Japan for an 8-and-6 victory to win the U.S. Women's Amateur.

images.name: Asterisk Talley [600x600]
images.caption: Asterisk Talley led 3 up after the opening 18, then poured it on in the afternoon to close out her match against Anna Iwanaga on the 12th hole.

receivedItems.headline: Carlos Alcaraz dominates Frances Tiafoe in ATP Finals opener
receivedItems.description: Third-ranked Carlos Alcaraz kept up his strong end-of-the season form with a dominant 6-2, 6-2 victory over Frances Tiafoe in his opening match at the ATP Finals on Monday.

receivedItems.headline: Alexander Zverev starts ATP Finals with convincing win over Rafael Jodar
receivedItems.description: Aiming to punctuate the best year of his career with another big title, top-ranked Alexander Zverev got his ATP Finals campaign off to a strong start with a 6-4, 6-4 victory over debutant Rafael Jodar.

receivedItems.headline: ATP Finals preview: Can Alcaraz close out the year with a big win?
receivedItems.description: Alcaraz has returned from injury and is on a hot streak, while Americans Shelton and Tiafoe are hoping to challenge for the ATP Finals title.

images.name: Carlos Alcaraz [1296x729]
images.caption: Carlos Alcaraz won the Paris Masters on Sunday, and the Vienna Open the week before.

images.name: Novak Djokovic [1296x729] - Copy
images.caption: Novak Djokovic missed out on qualifying for the ATP Finals, in what would have been a record-setting 19th appearance.

images.name: Zverev Shelton feature lede [1296x729] - Copy (2)
images.caption: Alexander Zverev won two major titles this season, and Ben Shelton made his first major final appearance.

images.name: Jodar celeb Madrid Open_260422 [1296x729] - Copy
images.caption: Rafael Jodar began 2026 ranked No. 168 in the world -- and is now ranked No. 9.

receivedItems.headline: Waiting game pays off for Tiafoe as he heads into ATP Finals
receivedItems.description: At 28, Frances Tiafoe has played in just about every tournament on tour. But this will be his first experience in the ATP Finals.

images.name: Frances Tiafoe ATP Finals [1296x729]
images.caption: Frances Tiafoe will play in his first ATP Finals, beginning on Sunday in Turin, Italy.

images.name: Ben Shelton and Frances Tiafoe [1296x729] - Copy
images.caption: Tiafoe made it to the US Open semifinals in September, before losing to Ben Shelton.

receivedItems.headline: Jannik Sinner (knee) plans return at Saudi exhibition in Aussie prep
receivedItems.description: Jannik Sinner, who has not played since July with a knee injury, said Tuesday he aims to return at an exhibition in Saudi Arabia in late December.

receivedItems.headline: Carlos Alcaraz beats Ben Shelton to win Paris Masters title
receivedItems.description: Carlos Alcaraz won his second straight title and fifth of the year with a straight-sets victory over Ben Shelton in the Paris Masters final.

images.name: Carlos Alcaraz [1296x729]
images.alt: Carlos Alcaraz

receivedItems.headline: Carlos Alcaraz looking for 'revenge' against Ben Shelton in Paris Masters final
receivedItems.description: Carlos Alcaraz reached his third final since the US Open when he beat Casper Ruud 6-4, 6-4 at the Paris Masters. Alcaraz will play Ben Shelton for the title.

images.name: Shelton Alcaraz feature lede [600x400]
images.caption: Ben Shelton defeated Carlos Alcaraz in the US Open quarterfinals -- becoming the first American to defeat Alcaraz at a major.

receivedItems.headline: Gaël Monfils stays in tennis as captain of France's Davis Cup team
receivedItems.description: Gaël Monfils will stay in tennis as captain of France's Davis Cup team, the national federation said.

receivedItems.headline: Alcaraz, Shelton into Paris Masters semis; ATP Finals field set
receivedItems.description: Carlos Alcaraz held off Taylor Fritz and Ben Shelton outlasted Tommy Paul to reach the Paris Masters semifinals while also finalizing the field for the ATP Finals.

receivedItems.headline: Ben Shelton tops Tommy Paul to reach first Paris Masters semifinal
receivedItems.description: Ben Shelton won an all-American matchup against Tommy Paul on Friday to reach the semifinals of the Paris Masters for the first time.

receivedItems.headline: Jannik Sinner replacing Darren Cahill with Magnus Norman on coaching team
receivedItems.description: Jannik Sinner's partnership with coach Darren Cahill is ending after a spell that saw the Italian win five Grand Slam titles and achieve the No. 1 ranking.

images.name: Jannik Sinner of Italy celebrates with his coach Darren Cahill  [600x400]

receivedItems.headline: Ben Shelton moves into Paris Masters quarters, to face Tommy Paul next
receivedItems.description: Ben Shelton beat Arthur Rinderknech 3-6, 6-4, 7-6 (5) on Thursday for a season's best 43rd win and a spot in the Paris Masters quarterfinals. The US Open runner-up next faces No. 12 Tommy Paul in an all-American contest.

images.name: Ben Shelton [600x400]
images.credit: Photo by Mustafa Yalcin/Anadolu via Getty Images

receivedItems.headline: Alexander Zverev loses first match as No. 1; Novak Djokovic also out in Paris
receivedItems.description: Alexander Zverev's tenure as the No. 1 player in men's tennis started with a 7-6 (5), 6-2 defeat to Lorenzo Musetti, while Novak Djokovic saw his dwindling hopes of making the ATP Finals with a loss to qualifier Rinky Hijikata.

images.name: Alexander Zverev [1296x729] - Copy
images.caption: Alexander Zverev became world No. 1 on Monday.

receivedItems.headline: Novak Djokovic fends off Valentin Vacherot at Paris Masters
receivedItems.description: Seven-time champion Novak Djokovic overcame a scare late in the second set to beat big-serving Valentin Vacherot in the first round of the Paris Masters.

receivedItems.headline: FAQ: Why Zverev's rise to world No. 1 provokes mixed feelings
receivedItems.description: Alexander Zverev's climb to No. 1 presents a complicated scenario for fans, sponsors and media due to his history of domestic violence allegations.

images.name: Alexander Zverev [1296x729] - Copy
images.caption: Alexander Zverev became world No. 1 on Monday.

images.name: Zverev Shelton feature lede [1296x729] - Copy
images.caption: Zverev defeated Ben Shelton in the US Open final in September.

images.name: Zverev Sinner [1296x729] - Copy
images.caption: Zverev is not likely to remain No. 1 long, as Jannik Sinner (pictured) and Carlos Alcaraz return to full health.

images.name: Alexander Zverev French Open [1296x729] - Copy
images.caption: Zverev won the first major title of his career at the French Open in June.

receivedItems.headline: Alexander Zverev rises to No. 1 men's tennis ranking after dominant season
receivedItems.description: Alexander Zverev rose to No. 1 in the men's tennis ranking after a dominant season in which he won the French and US Open titles.

images.name: Alexander Zverev French Open [1296x729] - Copy (2) 20261102
images.caption: Zverev won the first major title of his career at the French Open in June.

receivedItems.headline: Ben Shelton adds coach Juan Carlos Ferrero to 2027 staff
receivedItems.description: Carlos Alcaraz's former coach Juan Carlos Ferrero is joining Ben Shelton's coaching staff for the 2027 season.

receivedItems.headline: Valentin Vacherot rallies to beat Jiri Lehecka to win Swiss Indoors title
receivedItems.description: Valentin Vacherot clinched his second career title after beating Jiri Lehecka 2-6, 6-3, 6-3 in the Swiss Indoors final.

receivedItems.headline: Carlos Alcaraz beats Alex de Minaur to win Vienna Open for fourth title of 2026
receivedItems.description: Carlos Alcaraz beat Alex de Minaur 6-1, 6-4 to win the Vienna Open and defeat his opponent for the seventh time in as many meetings.

receivedItems.headline: Novak Djokovic loses to Jan-Lennard Struff at Swiss Indoors
receivedItems.description: Novak Djokovic had a tough loss Thursday at the Swiss Indoors, going down 6-7 (4), 7-5, 7-6 (5) to 47th-ranked Jan-Lennard Struff. He remains one career title behind Roger Federer's 103.

receivedItems.headline: Alexander Zverev's first No. 1 ranking to be confirmed Monday with win in Vienna
receivedItems.description: Alexander Zverev will finally rise to be the No. 1 men's tennis player Monday when the next rankings are published.

receivedItems.headline: Stan Wawrinka retires as Basel farewell ends in 1st-round loss
receivedItems.description: Stan Wawrinka's illustrious tennis career finally came to an end on Tuesday at his home tournament in Basel.

receivedItems.headline: Retired Rafael Nadal to play in Las Vegas exhibition in February
receivedItems.description: Rafael Nadal, winner of 22 Grand Slam titles, will play in a tennis exhibition in Las Vegas early next year, his first time playing in the U.S. since retiring two years ago.

images.name: Rafael Nadal [600x400]
images.caption: Five-time champion Rafael Nadal lost in the Round of 16 at the Madrid Open.

receivedItems.headline: Davidovich Fokina upsets Zverev, faces Jodar for Shanghai title
receivedItems.description: Alejandro Davidovich Fokina upset future No. 1 Alexander Zverev 5-7, 6-4, 6-3 to reach the Shanghai Masters final, where he will face 20-year-old Rafael Jodar.

receivedItems.headline: Rafael Jodar makes Shanghai Masters history, sets up semifinal vs. Medvedev
receivedItems.description: Rafael Jodar, 20, became the youngest semifinalist in Shanghai Masters history and will next meet Daniil Medvedev.

receivedItems.headline: Proposed ATP Tour changes address player welfare, compensation
receivedItems.description: The ATP Tour is proposing several rule changes in an effort to address player welfare, additional compensation, and enhancing pension and retirement benefits.

receivedItems.headline: Alexander Zverev wins in straight sets to reach Shanghai Masters semifinals
receivedItems.description: Top-ranked Alexander Zverev said he felt good on-court after beating Alex de Minaur 6-4, 6-4 at the Shanghai Masters.

receivedItems.headline: Drug-testing agency lists Monfils as retired, seemingly ruling out Paris farewell
receivedItems.description: French tennis player Gael Monfils has entered retirement, a move that came a bit earlier than what was expected.

receivedItems.headline: Medvedev beats longtime rival Tsitsipas, reaches Shanghai Masters quarterfinals
receivedItems.description: Daniil Medvedev is back in the Shanghai Masters quarterfinals after getting the better of Stefanos Tsitsipas in the latest chapter of their longtime rivalry.

receivedItems.headline: Zverev beats Bublik to reach Shanghai Masters quarters
receivedItems.description: Alexander Zverev beat Alexander Bublik 7-6 (6), 4-6, 7-6 (1) to reach the Shanghai Masters quarterfinals on Tuesday in his first match since securing the year-end No. 1 ranking.

receivedItems.headline: Zverev snags No. 1 ranking with Alcaraz loss, Sinner injury
receivedItems.description: Alexander Zverev, 29, who won his first two Grand Slam titles this year, has clinched the year-end No. 1 men's tennis ranking.

images.name: Alexander Zverev captures first US Open title of his career
images.caption: Alexander Zverev captures first US Open title of his career

receivedItems.headline: Zizou Bergs stuns Carlos Alcaraz in straight sets in Shanghai
receivedItems.description: Zizou Bergs stunned second-seeded Carlos Alcaraz 7-5, 7-6 (4) on Monday to advance to the fourth round of the Shanghai Masters.

receivedItems.headline: Ben Shelton stumbles in straight sets, Zverev wins in Shanghai
receivedItems.description: Ben Shelton lost 7-6 (5), 7-6 (3) to 21-year-old Frenchman Arthur Gea in the third round of the Shanghai Masters, while Alexander Zverev continued his push for the No. 1 ranking with a win.

receivedItems.headline: Carlos Alcaraz tests new mustache in opening Shanghai win
receivedItems.description: Carlos Alcaraz sported a mustache along with his team in the stands as he swept to a 6-3, 6-3 victory over Juan Manuel Cerundolo at the Shanghai Masters.

images.name: 261010 alcaraz photo [1296x729]
images.caption: Carlos Alcaraz said the mustache was a result of his title victory at the Japan Open.

receivedItems.headline: Novak Djokovic beaten by Hubert Hurkacz at Shanghai Masters
receivedItems.description: Novak Djokovic was knocked out of the Shanghai Masters after a shock second-round loss to Hubert Hurkacz on Friday.

receivedItems.headline: Shelton breezes to straight-sets win to advance in Shanghai
receivedItems.description: On his 24th birthday, Ben Shelton defeated Daniel Altmaier 6-3, 7-6 (6) to advance to the third round of the Shanghai Masters.

receivedItems.headline: Djokovic to reach out to Sinner about returning from long layoff
receivedItems.description: Novak Djokovic plans to reach out to Jannik Sinner after an injury ended the top-ranked player's season, saying Thursday he knows how difficult it is to come back after a lengthy layoff.

images.name: Djokovic and Sinner preview lede [600x400]
images.caption: Jannik Sinner, 24, will take on Novak Djokovic, 39, on Friday at Wimbledon.

receivedItems.headline: Alcaraz: Tennis schedule is pushing players too hard
receivedItems.description: Alcaraz: Tennis schedule is pushing players too hard

images.name: Alcaraz: Tennis schedule is pushing players too hard
images.caption: Alcaraz: Tennis schedule is pushing players too hard

receivedItems.headline: Tsitsipas advances in Shanghai; Hurkacz lines up Djokovic
receivedItems.description: Two-time major finalist Stefanos Tsitsipas beat Kimmer Coppejans in the Shanghai Masters first round to continue his slow climb back up the ATP rankings, while Hubert Hurkacz had 19 aces in a win over James Duckworth and next plays Novak Djokovic.

receivedItems.headline: Djokovic wins 7th China Open title after injured De Minaur retires
receivedItems.description: Novak Djokovic won his 7th China Open title Tuesday after Alex de Minaur retired in the second set of the final with a groin injury.

receivedItems.headline: Carlos Alcaraz retains Japan Open title in big step following injury layoff
receivedItems.description: Third-ranked Carlos Alcaraz beat Jiri Lehecka on Tuesday to defend his Japan Open title, in his second tournament back from an injury layoff.

receivedItems.headline: Jannik Sinner to miss rest of year due to knee inflammation
receivedItems.description: Jannik Sinner, who already announced he'd miss the Shanghai Masters, announced Tuesday he would miss the rest of the year due to knee inflammation.

receivedItems.headline: Medvedev out of China Open after smashing ball in fan's face
receivedItems.description: Daniil Medvedev was disqualified from his semifinal China Open match against Novak Djokovic after hitting a ball into the stands and striking a fan in the head. Djokovic advances to the final Tuesday vs. Alex de Minaur.

images.name: Daniil Medvedev DQ'd after hitting ball into stands that strikes spectator's face
images.caption: Daniil Medvedev DQ'd after hitting ball into stands that strikes spectator's face

receivedItems.headline: No. 3 Alcaraz overcomes big deficit to reach Japan Open final
receivedItems.description: No. 3-ranked Carlos Alcaraz overcame losing 16 straight points to beat Jaume Munar 5-7, 6-3, 6-1 to make the Japan Open final. It will be Alcaraz's first final since coming back from a 4 1/2-month layoff for a wrist injury.

images.name: Carlos Alcaraz [1296x729]
images.caption: 2026 Japan Open semis

receivedItems.headline: Carlos Alcaraz advances to Tokyo semis after Shapovalov injury
receivedItems.description: Carlos Alcaraz moved into the final four at the Tokyo Open after his quarterfinal opponent, Denis Shapovalov, was forced to retire due to a hip injury.

receivedItems.headline: Sinner extends absence by withdrawing from Shanghai Masters
receivedItems.description: Top-ranked Jannik Sinner has withdrawn from the Shanghai Masters as he deals with a knee problem.

images.name: Jannik Sinner of Italy plays a backhand against Alexander Zverev of Germany during their Gentlemen's Singles final match photodesk [600x400]

receivedItems.headline: Alcaraz beats Arnaldi to reach 3rd round at Japan Open
receivedItems.description: Top-seeded Carlos Alcaraz beat Matteo Arnaldi 7-6 (6), 6-1 on Saturday in a second-round match at the Japan Open, continuing his strong return to play after a four-month layoff due to a wrist injury.

receivedItems.headline: Novak Djokovic rallies, improves to 31-0 at China Open
receivedItems.description: Novak Djokovic rallied to beat Bu Yunchaokete to reach the quarterfinals and maintain his flawless record at the China Open despite again needing a medical timeout.

images.name: 261002 Djokovic [1296x729]
images.caption: Novak Djokovic rallied for a 4-6, 7-6 (2), 6-2 victory over Bu Yunchaokete to improve to 31-0 all-time at the China Open.

receivedItems.headline: Novak Djokovic starts China Open with first win since July
receivedItems.description: Novak Djokovic maintained his flawless record at the China Open despite needing a medical timeout during his first round match on Wednesday.

receivedItems.headline: Alexander Zverev locks up Laver Cup title for Team Europe
receivedItems.description: Alexander Zverev clinched the decisive points that brought the Laver Cup back to Team Europe.

images.alt: Alexander Zverev

receivedItems.headline: What does the future hold for the WTA Finals?
receivedItems.description: After six host cities in seven years, the WTA Finals will enter a new era of stability for the marquee year-end event.

images.name: Mirra Andreeva WTA Finals lede [1296x729]
images.caption: Mirra Andreeva won the WTA Finals title match on Sunday, in Indian Wells, California.

images.name: Elina Svitolina [1296x729] - Copy
images.caption: No. 6-ranked Elina Svitolina was the runner-up to Andreeva, and was back at the Finals for the first time since 2019.

receivedItems.headline: Mirra Andreeva beats Elina Svitolina to win WTA Finals without losing a set
receivedItems.description: Mirra Andreeva defeated Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 to win the WTA Finals on Sunday without dropping a set over five matches at the season-ending championships.

images.name: Mirra Andreeva [600x400]
images.caption: Mirra Andreeva became the 11th player to win the WTA Finals without losing a set, joining among others Chris Evert, Martina Navratilova and Serena Williams, all of whom did it multiple times.

receivedItems.headline: Sabalenka sorry for on-court outburst in loss to Svitolina, says fans upset her
receivedItems.description: Aryna Sabalenka apologized for an on-court outburst in her three-set loss to Elina Svitolina at the WTA Finals, saying it was directed at a group of fans.

receivedItems.headline: Mirra Andreeva is 1st teen in WTA Finals title match since Maria Sharapova
receivedItems.description: Mirra Andreeva defeated Jessica Pegula 6-3, 6-4 to reach the WTA Finals title match. Elina Svitolina routed Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova 6-2, 6-1 in the other semifinal.

receivedItems.headline: Katerina Siniakova clinches record 6th year-end WTA No. 1 doubles finish
receivedItems.description: Katerina Siniakova has clinched her record sixth year-end finish as the world's top-ranked doubles player on the WTA Tour.

receivedItems.headline: Elina Svitolina beats Aryna Sabalenka in 3 sets to reach semis at WTA Finals
receivedItems.description: Elina Svitolina overcame Aryna Sabalenka 6-3, 3-6, 6-1 to reach the semifinals of the WTA Finals on Friday, winning on her fourth match point.

receivedItems.headline: Karolina Muchova withdraws from WTA Finals due to illness
receivedItems.description: Karolina Muchova withdrew from the WTA Finals on Friday with a gastrointestinal illness.

images.name: Karolina Muchova [1296x729]
images.alt: Karolina Muchova

receivedItems.headline: Jessica Pegula advances in 3 sets at WTA Finals, ousting Coco Gauff
receivedItems.description: Jessica Pegula fired a career-high 16 aces to advance to the semifinals of the WTA Finals in a three-set win against Linda Noskova, knocking out Coco Gauff from the $10 million, season-ending competition.

receivedItems.headline: Mirra Andreeva beats Aryna Sabalenka in straight sets to reach WTA Finals semis
receivedItems.description: Mirra Andreeva won her WTA Finals round-robin group in emphatic fashion Wednesday, defeating Aryna Sabalenka 6-4, 6-0.

receivedItems.headline: Linda Noskova reaches WTA Finals semis with win over Coco Gauff
receivedItems.description: Linda Noskova became the first to qualify for the semifinal round of the WTA Finals, defeating Coco Gauff 6-3, 6-3 in 1 hour and 15 minutes on Tuesday.

receivedItems.headline: Aryna Sabalenka picks up first win at WTA Finals, faces Mirra Andreeva next
receivedItems.description: Aryna Sabalenka defeated Karolina Muchova 7-6 (2), 7-5 for her first win at the 2026 WTA Finals on Monday. The former world No. 1 will next face No. 3 seed Mirra Andreeva.

receivedItems.headline: Coco Gauff opens 2026 WTA Finals with win vs. Jessica Pegula
receivedItems.description: Coco Gauff defeated fellow American Jessica Pegula 6-4, 6-7 (5), 6-2 in her first match of the 2026 WTA Finals on Sunday.

receivedItems.headline: American Claire Liu wins Hong Kong Tennis Open for her 1st career WTA title
receivedItems.description: American Claire Liu defeated Alexandra Eala 6-3, 6-0 to win the Hong Kong Tennis Open for her first WTA title.

receivedItems.headline: No. 1 Elena Rybakina withdraws from WTA Finals for medical reasons
receivedItems.description: Top-ranked Elena Rybakina has withdrawn from the WTA Finals for medical reasons before the season-ending championships begin.

receivedItems.headline: Alex Eala outlasts Maria Sakkari in rain-soaked Hong Kong Open semifinals, faces Claire Liu in final
receivedItems.description: This puts Eala one win away from claiming her second WTA Tour title of the year.

receivedItems.headline: Jessica Pegula: Hot mic comments about Mirra Andreeva an 'unfortunate situation'
receivedItems.description: Tennis star Jessica Pegula told ESPN on Friday that her hot mic comments about Mirra Andreeva were an "unfortunate situation," before adding that the matter has been handled "privately."

receivedItems.headline: Alex Eala survives Antonia Ruzic test, storms into Hong Kong Open semifinals against Maria Sakkari
receivedItems.description: After surviving a tense opening-set tiebreak, the Filipina shifted into another gear to dismantle Croatia's Antonia Ruzic, 7-6(7), 7-5, and advance to the Hong Kong Open semifinals.

receivedItems.description: Elena Rybakina and Aryna Sabalenka head their respective singles groups for the WTA Finals, with Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula landing in the same group.

receivedItems.description: Despite a late change in opponent, Alex Eala was still able to comfortably breeze through her opening match at the Hong Kong Open.

receivedItems.headline: Venus Williams loses in Guangzhou Open doubles semifinals
receivedItems.description: Venus Williams and Janice Tjen lost to Polina Kudermetova and Maria Timofeeva 6-4, 6-7 (8), 10-6 in the Guangzhou Open doubles semifinals.

images.caption: Venus Williams served for 14 1/2 minutes in the penultimate game of her Australian Open first-round match against Olga Danilovic, who ultimately got the final break.

receivedItems.headline: Leylah Fernandez advances to Tokyo WTA final with win over Rakhimova
receivedItems.description: Leylah Fernandez has advanced to her third WTA final of the year, with a chance to win her second tournament.

receivedItems.headline: Elena Rybakina withdraws from Pan Pacific Open quarterfinals, citing injury
receivedItems.description: Elena Rybakina, the world's No. 1-ranked player and top seed in the Pan Pacific Open, withdrew from her quarterfinal match on Friday, handing the win to Leylah Fernandez of Canada.

receivedItems.headline: Naomi Osaka ousted from Tokyo tournament by 18-year-old Mia Pohankova
receivedItems.description: Four-time major winner Naomi Osaka lost in front of her home crowd to Slovakian teenager Mia Pohankova in the Pan Pacific Open round of 16.

receivedItems.headline: Alex Eala rallies past Talia Gibson, sets up Diana Shnaider rematch in Toray Pan Pacific Open quarterfinals
receivedItems.description: Alex Eala is through to the Toray Pan Pacific Open quarterfinals after coming from behind to beat Talia Gibson.

images.caption: Alex Eala is through to the Toray Pan Pacific Open quarterfinals after coming from behind to beat Talia Gibson 4-6, 6-2, 6-0.

receivedItems.headline: Naomi Osaka moves into 2nd round in Tokyo, in front of home fans
receivedItems.description: In front of her home fans, Naomi Osaka defeated Jasmine Paolini on Tuesday to advance to the second round of the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo.

receivedItems.headline: First-round loss in China drops Venus Williams to 0-13 in singles
receivedItems.description: With a loss to Lilli Tagger, 18, in the Guangzhou Open on Tuesday, Venus Williams is now 0-13 in singles matches this year.

receivedItems.headline: Alex Eala claims dominant opening win over Mika Stojsavljevic at Toray Pan Pacific Open
receivedItems.description: Alex Eala has made a dominant start to the Toray Pan Pacific Open, seeing off Mika Stojsavljevic 6-1, 6-2.

images.name: Alex Eala [1296x729]
images.caption: Alex Eala has made a strong start at the Toray Pan Pacific Open after cruising to a 6-1, 6-2 win over Mika Stojsavljevic on Monday.

receivedItems.headline: Katerina Siniakova breezes past Ashlyn Krueger to win Japan Open
receivedItems.description: Katerina Siniakova defeated Ashlyn Kreuger 6-1, 6-0 to win the Japan Open for her first singles title in three years.

receivedItems.headline: Top-ranked Elena Rybakina avoids upset at Ningbo Open
receivedItems.description: Top-ranked Elena Rybakina avoided a major upset as she was pushed to a deciding set by qualifier Katarzyna Kawa in the quarterfinals of the Ningbo Open.

images.name: Elena Rybakina feature lede [600x400]
images.caption: Elena Rybakina won the US Open title on Saturday over two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka.

receivedItems.headline: Alex Eala falls to Diana Shnaider in tight Ningbo Open round of 16 clash
receivedItems.description: Alex Eala was eliminated from the Ningbo Open round of 16 by world No. 13 Diana Shnaider on Thursday.

images.caption: Alex Eala is out of the Ningbo Open after suffering a straight sets loss to world No. 13 Diana Shnaider in the round of 16 on Thursday.

receivedItems.headline: Kostyuk retires from Ningbo match, handing last WTA Finals slot to Muchova
receivedItems.description: Marta Kostyuk retired from her second-round match at the Ningbo Open on Wednesday, handing Karolina Muchova the last spot in the season-ending WTA Finals.

receivedItems.headline: Iga Swiatek out of Ningbo Open with thigh injury; may lose shot at Indian Wells
receivedItems.description: Iga Swiatek has withdrawn from the Ningbo Open in China due to a nagging thigh injury and is in jeopardy to make the season-ending Indian Wells tournament roster.

receivedItems.headline: Alex Eala snaps three-match skid, cruises past Diane Parry at Ningbo Open
receivedItems.description: Alex Eala has snapped a three-match losing streak to get off to a winning start at the Ningbo Open.

images.name: Alex Eala [1296x729]
images.caption: Alex Eala got off to a winning start at the Ningbo Open on Monday with a 6-3, 6-1 win over Diane Parry.

receivedItems.description: Sonay Kartal's quest for a first WTA 1000 triumph fell short on Sunday as she was beaten 6, 2, 4-6, 6-2 by Maja Chwalińska at the Wuhan Open.

receivedItems.description: Elise Mertens beat her third Grand Slam winner during her China Open run, besting Iga Swiatek in straight sets to reach the semifinals in Beijing.

receivedItems.headline: Andreeva, Bartunkova reach China Open semis with straight-set wins
receivedItems.description: Mirra Andreeva and Nikola Bartunkova advanced to the semifinals of the China Open with straight-sets victories Thursday in Beijing.

receivedItems.headline: Coco Gauff says abuse 'draining' after first loss to Mertens
receivedItems.description: Coco Gauff lost to Elise Mertens, whom she had beaten in all five of their previous matchups, before saying she felt drained over the abusive comments she received during the China Open.

receivedItems.headline: Nikola Bartunkova wins again, Naomi Osaka ousted at China Open
receivedItems.description: Nikola Bartunkova's run at the China Open continues after defeating Sinja Kraus on Tuesday in three sets to advance to the quarterfinals in Beijing.

receivedItems.headline: Coco Gauff: 'Insane' amount of racist comments after match
receivedItems.description: After a disputed point in her win over Sun Xinran at the China Open on Monday, Coco Gauff said she received an "insane" amount of racist comments.

receivedItems.description: US Open semifinalist Coco Gauff beat Camila Osorio 7-6 (4), 4-6, 6-2 in a second-round match at the China Open, while No. 1-ranked Elena Rybakina was ousted by No. 118 Alina Charaeva.

receivedItems.description: Novak Djokovic rallied to beat Bu Yunchaokete to reach the quarterfinals and maintain his flawless record at the China Open despite again needing a medical timeout.
